title: Minimum Cost for Cutting Cake I
summary: Given an m x n cake that needs to be cut into 1 x 1 pieces, you are provided with two arrays: horizontalCut of size m - 1, where each element represents the cost to cut along a specific horizontal line, and verticalCut of size n - 1, where each element represents the cost to cut along a specific vertical line.
statement: Given an m x n cake that needs to be cut into 1 x 1 pieces, you are provided with two arrays: horizontalCut of size m - 1, where each element represents the cost to cut along a specific horizontal line, and verticalCut of size n - 1, where each element represents the cost to cut along a specific vertical line. In one operation, you can choose any piece of cake that is not yet a 1 x 1 square and perform a cut along either a horizontal line (at a cost specified in horizontalCut) or a vertical line (at a cost specified in verticalCut). After the cut, the piece of cake is divided into two distinct pieces. The cost of each cut is fixed and does not change. The task is to determine the minimum total cost required to cut the entire cake into 1 x 1 pieces.
constraints: horizontalCut and verticalCut have lengths m-1 and n-1 and contain positive costs.
A cut is applied separately to every existing piece it crosses, always charging its listed cost.
Return the minimum total cost to produce all 1x1 pieces; this version uses a small-grid order DP.
hints: Only how many horizontal and vertical cuts have occurred affects the multiplier of the next cut.
Sort costs descending within each direction and use DP over counts taken from both lists.
Transition by next horizontal cost*(verticalPieces) or next vertical cost*(horizontalPieces).
An exchange argument fixes descending order within each orientation, while DP enumerates every interleaving of those two fixed orders.
